KZN KILLING FIELDS

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
With political position comes power, even at grassroots level. We investigate a spate of execution style hit behind the killing of at least 27 KZN Izindunas where life appears to be cheap.

Unique Selling Point:
** INTERVIEW WITH INKABI
** UNDERCOVER INVESTIGATION OF EASE WITH WHICH GUNS ARE OBTAINED ILLEGALLY FOR THESE HITS

Summary:
KZN is notorious for it’s hitmen that will pull the trigger for a price. At least 27 KZN izindunas have killed while several others have escaped assassination attempts since January 2019. THE MOTIVE? CONTENTION OVER TRADITIONAL LEADERSHIP POSITIONS.

With upcoming local elections and the death of the Zulu King, this is the perfect time to look at an underworld of Izinkabi – KZN’s notorius hitmen that have been linked to the murder of underworld attorney Mihalik in 2018, taxi wars and other political killings.

We explore the phenomenon of KZN’s Izinkabi and investigate the trail of dead chiefs.


Further information:
WHY DO IT NOW
- Current new angle
- Upcoming Local Elections

SEXY ELEMENTS
- brutal execution style hits / ambush-style shootings
- inside look into underworld
- supported by research

This story is the stuff movies are made of but with a truly South African twists - taxi bosses, izinkabi and political problem people being taken out like murder is a way of life.

TARGETS: TRADITIONAL LEADERS
LOCATION: KZN
WHY NOW: 2021 LOCAL ELECTIONS – FOR THE LAST TWO YEARS, BEING AN INDUNA COMES WITH CASH.

THE MOTIVE? CONTENTION OVER TRADITIONAL LEADERSHIP POSITIONS.
1. MONEY - Izindunas are paid a R10 000 monthly stipend that the provincial government stated paying them about two years ago.
2. POSITION – Some izindunas were caught in the crossfire of factional battles over chieftaincy.

INDUANA PHAKAMANI DLAMINI – is the secreatary of Ubumbano Lwezinduna which is an association of izindumna with 3000 members across the province.
“We are being butchered every single day abut no one has ever been prosecutred for killing an induna. It’s become clear to us that we are on our own and each of us is just waiting for the day the gunmen knocks on our front door. Even with political violence we didn’t see so many people slaughered like this.”

Most of the Izindunas who have been killed either received death threats, were harrased or there were attempts to unseat them before the gunmen visited their homes.

Dlamini says the organisation has raised alarm with local authorities each time there have been threaths to a indunas and yet he claims nothing has been done.




INTERVIEWS
- INDUANA PHAKAMANI DLAMINI from Ubumbano Lwezinduna
- FAMILY OF KILLED INDUNA
- GREG ARDE – RESEARCHED KZN HITMEN IN THE TAXI UNDERWORLD LINKED TO THE ANC POLITICAL SPHERE
- SHAHEEN SULIMAN - CRIME EXPERT
- POSSIBLE HITMAN – HIDDEN ID

SOME HITS
NOVEMBER 2020 – Prince Hlabisa frm uMkhanyakude was shot in front of his grandchildren who were around ages 7 & 8.
JANUARY 2021 – Bonginkosi Dlomo was shot 12 times in an ambush-style attack in Mpophomeni and Bongumusa Mdluli was gunned down in KwaManyavy.

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: No province in South Africa is immune to political killings, but the terror of assassinations that’s become synonymous with KwaZulu Natal’s volatile political landscape – is unmatched.

XOLANI: In a way, we live in a Columbian kind of a state where the underworld ends up running the normal world.

VO Political Commentator Xolani Dube explains that the issues are complex and murky as politics, corruption and crime have become integrated.

XOLANI: KwaZulu-Natal is very violent because people were at the helm. They use violence for their own survival and for their own livelihood

LINK: With Power positions comes a certain stature, respect and influence, but more recently, it also comes with a target on your back, even at grassroots level.

VO: Since 2019, at least 27 traditional leaders have been taken out in KwaZulu Natal.

DLAMINI: It's execution, it's brutal, it's bad…

VO: The fear is palpable. Induna Phakamani Dlamini has survived an assassination attempt. Representing 3000 traditional leaders across KZN, he says there’s no doubt that these murders are hits.

DLAMINI: They make sure that they don't deliver anything in your house. They just come and kill you in front of everyone. Then they will only kill you and go away.

VO: This is the work of izinkabi – it is the Zulu term for hitmen – they are notorious in KZN – pulling the trigger for a price.

This man is a so-called inkabi. Although he claims to have retired from brutally killing people for payment, he also claims to have done many hits, having started his reign of terror in the early nineties.

MAC: Do you remember a number?
INKABI: I can’t give you a number because I wasn’t counting you see

VO: Today he works as a security informant, selling information. He has moved into the taxi industry as a taxi boss.

Izinkabi like mercenaries, are focussed on making money, often at the expense of ethics, reflects Dube.

XOLANI: In the end, mercenaries and soldiers and hitmen, they perform the same responsibility or the same job is to kill on behalf of those who have hired.

INKABI: There’s lots of work, Tenders, politician and taxi. The reason there are these murders, is because people want to own everything – people don’t want to share.

VO: Traditional leaders are targets, now that they get a R10 000 monthly stipend from the government. Everybody wants in, explains Dlamini.

DLAMINI: We believe that it's over positions now that we are getting paid, people have interest on our positions. Each and every people. Now they do like to become is an induna.
XOLANI: it is easy to to say, let me simply terminate this other person so that I can be part of of those who are enjoying this kind of livelihood.

LINK: This area has been plagued by threats and attacks against traditional leaders, Bonginkosi Dlomo was one of them. While he was respected by some, others wanted him dead.

ZINHLE: All the threats were related to him being an induna – but he didn’t pay them any attention

VO: Zinhle Dlomo is Bonginkosi’s widow. He was gunned down at their home in Mphopomeni, in December 2020.

ZINHLE: It’s hard but I’m forced to accept the situation because I’m a mother. There are children I need to raise, I can’t let them see just how much pain I’m in, I have to pretend to be ok for them.

VO: Zinhle says on the day of his murder, her husband knew the threats were no longer empty.

ZINHLE: When we were driving, he told me there’s an inkabi that’s been paid to come kill me.

VO: The gunman came out of the shadows, fired 12 shots and fled the scene.

These attacks bring back memories of political violence in the early 90s for Dlamini.

DLAMINI: It's unfortunate that in such a beautiful province, we are exposed to violent again and it's easy to kill someone because you get away with murder and there's no arrest

VO: Reflecting on the heinous crimes the inkabi has committed, he is clear that getting caught is not of the slightest concern for hitmen like him.

INKABI: it’s hard to be scared of the police when the people you work for have money. In SA you’ll never see the inside of a cell if you have money

GREG: It's deeply troubling. It means that might is right, and murder hold sway.

VO: Investigative journalist Greg Arde explored how turf is won by physically eliminating rivals in his book War Party.

GREG: It reinforces the culture of violence in South Africa, if you have a breed of killers who work across platforms. You are cold blooded mercenaries who will do the bidding of the paymaster in a personal dispute, in a traditional dispute, in a in a taxi dispute or in or in a political contestation.

VO: Minister Bheki Cele recently held a media briefing on political killings in KZN.

CELE: What one thing about those killers you thought that they are killing for the taxi industry, they are killing for the political thing for robbery, that we have discovered that they're in one pool.

VO: Currently, the top three police stations for murder in the first quarter of the year, are all in KwaZulu-Natal. Plessislaer in Pietermaritzburg with 73, followed by Inanda with 63; and then Umlazi with 61 murder cases.

CELE: That tells us there is a problem that there is a special approach to killing in KZN. Even if you go to other provinces, people that are izinkabi that are causing problems…. trace them to the deep rural parts of this province.

VO: This video clip is of a hit in Pietermaritzburg. The shooting was allegedly linked to the drug world. Watch how brazen the shooters are – firing without hesitation in broad daylight.

The inkabi horrifically explained that the goal is simple, kill the target quickly and get out of there.

INKABI: I won't miss, because when I come for you, you’re not expecting me. I make sure to hit the lethal places so you don’t even make it to the hospital because if I miss my employer won’t pay me

XOLANI: It has evolved because it is a monetary value//they have commercialized their skills to make it appropriate for a capitalist society so that they can survive. And so it's a form of employment for them

VO: This inkabi arrogantly joked that it’s the only job he’s ever had - he now works for himself with the taxi’s he operates.

INKABI: I’ve never had to say good morning at a formal job
MAC: how do you become an inkabi
INKABI you have to ask yourself how much courage do you have? and it starts with hunger. Someone asks that you take a person out for them and they’ll pay 50k or 100k. Then it becomes clear to you, that you can take this person out for this amount of cash. because, see you don’t have a problem with them, your problem is that you need the money and this is how you get it

GREG: The problem is a massive culture of impunity, and we know that they can get away with it. Because these people are still out there and the killings are still continuing.

VO: The police are positive that progress is being made. The politically motivated murder rate has dropped significantly, but hitmen still continue to kill indiscriminately for whoever puts up the cash.

CELE: Those guys don't kill you because they hate you. They are killing for money. So that's an issue. They'll have to not just the footsoldiers, but who pays the money? Who is the boss who calls for this?

VO: Arde is convinced that following the money is key to stopping this crime trend.

GREG: It was the most frustrating thing in my research was everyone could reasonably easily establish who the killers were, but who was who was really pulling the levers?

VO: Investigator Shaheen Suliman has worked a number of these cases, while the paymasters are outside, the criminals calling the shots are often already doing time.

SHAHEEN: A lot of the crime in the network that happens happens with criminals being in prison //One robber speaks to the other robber.

VO: After a crime has been committed, weapons are recycled and traded between criminals - either sold or often hired out, explains Suliman.

SHAHEEN: Well, it look any anything from 500 range for a handgun to a thousand rand for AK 47
MAC: No, no ways that's an automatic rifle.
SHAHEEN: That's automatic rifle, 100 percent.

VO: The inkabi preferred to buy guns - he claims there’s no shortage of suppliers.

INKABI: Mostly from the police, from the robbery, if there’s robbery, there’s a gun they take it and sell it on to someone else.

VO: He made a call to demonstrate just how easy it is to get your hands on a gun.

INKABI: Can I come get it? How much must I bring?
SELLER: I’ve been waiting for your call, bring 3.5.
INKABI: 3.5
SELLER: I also have an AK if you want it?
INKABI: Oh really? An AK? How much do you want for the AK my brother?
SELLER: You can give me 6 or 5k for it

VO: As long as there are illegal guns available - the blood will continue to flow in KZN. Traditional Leaders are desperate for action.

DLAMINI: Each and every one of us is going through the same thing. Yeah. So I'm scared to go home and find people waiting for me there. It's not safe anymore.

VO: Minister Cele confirms that traditional leader shootings have gained momentum in recent months and need further investigation.

CELE: We need to we need to strategize and strategize a chasing these matters. One of the biggest formula is to work as a chain, work as the police, prosecution, magistracy and correctional services so that when they are there in corrections and they are kept there for a long time.,

VO: Arde believes the outlook is very grim if authorities don’t get on top of the driving forces behind KZN’s Killing Fields.

GREG: I think the way forward is to have really solid prosecution and keep these people behind bars if we don't, we're on the road to fully fledged gangster state.
MAC: And if nothing happens?
GREG: then you've got to seriously worry about driving home. Every night.

INKABI: this thing of inkabi will never end because the people inkabi work for have money. You can go anywhere in the world, even if the world ends, it won’t stop

XOLANI: what you see in this province is inkabi and so forth, and the direct product of greediness, incompetency and also self-serving of the so-called politicians. And so in a way, the real inkabi are the politicians.





PROMOS

PROMO 1: With political position comes power. We investigate a spate of hits that killed at least 27 Izindunas in KZN where life is seemingly cheap and illegal guns plentiful.

PROMO 2: Notorious for hired hitmen linked to taxi wars and political murders, KZN has seen 27 izindunas assassinated. We speak to a hitman who kills for cash.

PROMO 3: Izinkabi are the hitmen of KwaZulu-Natal’s underworld, We speak to one of them as we investigate what’s behind the brutal execution-style hits plaguing the province.

VO: Minister Cele confirms that traditional leader shootings have gained momentum in recent months and need further investigation. CELE: We need to we need to strategize and strategize a chasing these matters. One of the biggest formula is to work as a chain, work as the police, prosecution, magistracy and correctional services so that when they are there in corrections and they are kept there for a long time., VO: Arde believes the outlook is very grim if authorities don’t get on top of the driving forces behind KZN’s Killing Fields. GREG: I think the way forward is to have really solid prosecution and keep these people behind bars if we don't, we're on the road to fully fledged gangster state. MAC: And if nothing happens? GREG: then you've got to seriously worry about driving home. Every night. INKABI: this thing of inkabi will never end because the people inkabi work for have money. You can go anywhere in the world, even if the world ends, it won’t stop XOLANI: what you see in this province is inkabi and so forth, and the direct product of greediness, incompetency and also self-serving of the so-called politicians. And so in a way, the real inkabi are the politicians. PROMOS PROMO 1: With political position comes power. We investigate a spate of hits that killed at least 27 Izindunas in KZN where life is seemingly cheap and illegal guns plentiful. metadata.Summary: KZN is notorious for it’s hitmen that will pull the trigger for a price. At least 27 KZN izindunas have killed while several others have escaped assassination attempts since January 2019. THE MOTIVE? CONTENTION OVER TRADITIONAL LEADERSHIP POSITIONS. With upcoming local elections and the death of the Zulu King, this is the perfect time to look at an underworld of Izinkabi – KZN’s notorius hitmen that have been linked to the murder of underworld attorney Mihalik in 2018, taxi wars and other political killings. We explore the phenomenon of KZN’s Izinkabi and investigate the trail of dead chiefs.
metadata.Further information: WHY DO IT NOW - Current new angle - Upcoming Local Elections SEXY ELEMENTS - brutal execution style hits / ambush-style shootings - inside look into underworld - supported by research This story is the stuff movies are made of but with a truly South African twists - taxi bosses, izinkabi and political problem people being taken out like murder is a way of life. TARGETS: TRADITIONAL LEADERS LOCATION: KZN WHY NOW: 2021 LOCAL ELECTIONS – FOR THE LAST TWO YEARS, BEING AN INDUNA COMES WITH CASH. THE MOTIVE? CONTENTION OVER TRADITIONAL LEADERSHIP POSITIONS. 1. MONEY - Izindunas are paid a R10 000 monthly stipend that the provincial government stated paying them about two years ago. 2. POSITION – Some izindunas were caught in the crossfire of factional battles over chieftaincy. INDUANA PHAKAMANI DLAMINI – is the secreatary of Ubumbano Lwezinduna which is an association of izindumna with 3000 members across the province. “We are being butchered every single day abut no one has ever been prosecutred for killing an induna. It’s become clear to us that we are on our own and each of us is just waiting for the day the gunmen knocks on our front door. Even with political violence we didn’t see so many people slaughered like this.” Most of the Izindunas who have been killed either received death threats, were harrased or there were attempts to unseat them before the gunmen visited their homes. Dlamini says the organisation has raised alarm with local authorities each time there have been threaths to a indunas and yet he claims nothing has been done. JANUARY 2021 – Bonginkosi Dlomo was shot 12 times in an ambush-style attack in Mpophomeni and Bongumusa Mdluli was gunned down in KwaManyavy.
